## 固定收益開盤主論述

美國7月就業人數意外減少，加上先前月份數據大幅下修，顯示勞動市場原本就比初值疲弱，帶動美國公債於8月7日上漲。這份意外偏弱的報告降低了聯準會急於升息的必要性，但並未完全排除升息可能：2年期殖利率下跌5.3個基點至4.196%，5年期下跌4.4個基點至4.353%，10年期下跌3.5個基點至4.646%，30年期則下跌2.5個基點至5.202%。

短端反應較大，殖利率曲線因而轉陡。2年與10年期利差擴大1.8個基點至45個基點，2年與30年期利差擴大2.8個基點至100.6個基點。投資人將9月升息機率由就業報告公布前的近60%降至約40%，但仍完全反映年底前升息一次。這項差異顯示，就業數據削弱了立即緊縮的理由，通膨、財政供給及聯準會政策回應的公信力風險則仍集中在殖利率曲線較長端。

非農就業減少2.3萬人，遠遜於市場預期增加約8萬人，5月與6月數據合計下修10.3萬人。儘管如此，由於勞動參與率下降，失業率反而降至4.1%，薪資增幅則放緩。政府、休閒與旅宿及零售業均減少職位，使疲弱情況不只侷限於單一產業。里奇蒙聯準銀行總裁Tom Barkin形容勞動市場處於「疲弱的平衡」，並表示未見薪資通膨，但若價格壓力加劇，利率仍可能需要上調。

美國公債行情的組成也印證了這種有條件的解讀。10年期實質殖利率下降4個基點至2.392%，降幅超過名目殖利率，10年期損益兩平通膨率反而上升0.5個基點至2.254%。市場調低的是與成長及貨幣緊縮相關的實質利率路徑，並未獲得相當程度的通膨利多。荷莫茲海峽談判仍無結果，WTI上漲1.15%至$78.18，布蘭特原油上漲1.29%至$83.55，儘管兩者全週仍下跌逾7%。

風險性資產主要將招聘轉弱視為聯準會可以等待的理由，而非經濟正急遽萎縮的證據。標普500指數上漲0.62%至歷史新高，全週漲幅達3.58%；那斯達克100指數上漲1.19%，費城半導體指數上漲2.56%。美元指數下跌0.37%，黃金期貨則上漲2.33%至$4,340.70。公債殖利率在股市走強、油價上漲之際下降，顯示收盤行情的核心是政策預期重新定價，而非市場全面避險。

這波上漲並未解決長天期債券的問題。30年期殖利率仍高於5.2%，過去一個月上升14.5個基點，2年期同期僅上升0.9個基點。市場持續討論未來美國公債標售規模，科技業大量發債，加上伊朗衝突對通膨的影響仍不明朗，長端仍要求較高補償。就業報告改變了聯準會近期政策的計算，卻尚未決定長期資金應有的價格。

## 就業減少使聯準會重新審視勞動市場

7月就業報告實質改變了市場對勞動市場現況的衡量。非農就業減少2.3萬人，不只是低於預期增加約8萬人；5月與6月合計下修10.3萬人，也顯示先前的就業成長軌跡遭到高估，使最近三個月平均就業增幅降至約2萬人。這一連串數據令市場更難將7月結果視為單月波動。

產業細項顯示疲弱來源不只一處。政府就業下降，休閒與旅宿及零售業也裁減職位，意味職位流失並非集中在受到短期干擾的單一產業。不過，失業率降至4.1%，使這份報告尚不足以成為明確的衰退訊號。勞動參與率持續下降，計入勞動力的人數減少，也解釋了為何就業人數萎縮之際，失業率仍能改善。

薪資成長放緩，進一步支持勞動需求已不再帶來同等通膨壓力的看法。Barkin表示，這項結果符合約一年半以來的低招聘環境：勞動市場既不寬鬆，也不緊俏，而是處於疲弱的平衡。他未觀察到薪資通膨，也不認為目前就業狀況正在推升價格壓力。

但明年擁有政策投票權的Barkin，並未因此無條件反對升息。一週前，他曾表示借貸成本是否已高到足以抑制通膨仍難以判斷；週五又指出，如果通膨逆風加劇，官員可能仍須進一步緊縮。他的立場將市場近期經常合併看待的兩個問題分開：招聘疲弱降低勞動市場引發通膨的風險，卻不能保證能源、貿易成本或其他價格會回到目標。

短期利率的反應體現了這項區別。數據公布後，2年期殖利率一度下跌多達9個基點，終場跌幅收斂至5.3個基點。交易員將9月升息機率由報告公布前的近60%下調至約40%。與擔保隔夜融資利率連結的選擇權市場解除部分防範短率上升的避險部位，但投資人仍反映年底前升息一次，並保留防範2027年再次升息的部位。

市場仍反映年底前升息，既源於單月就業數據的不確定性，也反映通膨問題尚未解決。聯準會7月決定將目標區間維持在3.5%至3.75%時，有三名官員反對，主張升息25個基點。通膨仍高於2%目標，主席Kevin Warsh對於何種條件會使政策由按兵不動轉為升息，也幾乎未提供指引。非農就業數據使9月升息更難合理化，卻未說明通膨必須改善多少，決策委員會才會完全放棄進一步緊縮。

紐約聯準銀行7月消費者調查呈現更複雜的家庭觀點。受訪勞工認為失業後能找到新工作的機率升至46.2%，創今年最高；其中，高中或以下學歷者，以及年收入低於$5萬的家庭，升幅尤其顯著。然而，受訪者也提高了對一年後失業率上升的機率判斷，並認為自己失業的可能性略有增加。

家庭最短期的通膨預期小幅改善。一年期預期通膨率由3.7%降至3.6%，三年期與五年期則分別維持在3.3%與3%。表示目前財務狀況優於一年前的家庭增加，但認為未來三個月無法支付最低債務還款額的機率也上升，低收入家庭尤其明顯。這項調查早於非農就業報告，並未抵銷後者的訊號；它顯示消費者仍認為勞動市場存在工作機會，同時對整體前景更加擔憂。

貝萊德的Rick Rieder對非農就業下降提出了重要的不同解讀。他認為，招聘疲弱反映的是生產力轉型，而非經濟動能流失；人工智慧的採用、企業效率提升及移民減少，都可能使企業在不增加員工的情況下擴張。Rieder仍預期名目GDP成長約6%，並形容整體經濟表現平淡，但並不疲弱。

這項區別對政策相當重要，因為員工人數成長放緩，未必代表產出或需求會按相同比例流失。如果生產力讓企業能以較少員工生產更多，就業疲弱可能誇大實際經濟活動的惡化程度。Rieder也認為，提高隔夜利率並不適合抑制醫療、保險與教育等黏著性價格，財政及監管措施更為合適。他的判斷同時質疑傳統政策反應函數的兩端：就業報告未必顯示成長嚴重轉弱，再次升息也未必能直接處理持續通膨的來源。

跨市場表現較偏向這種溫和解讀。股市未因所得可能流失而下跌，反由科技與半導體股領漲；近期聯準會升息預期降溫，美元對所有主要貨幣走弱。信用債基金也小幅上漲，LQD漲0.18%、HYG漲0.19%、JNK漲0.21%、EMB漲0.31%。這些價格變動顯示，投資人認為聯準會可以保持耐心，對當日行情的重要性高於就業疲弱可能損及企業現金流的風險。

現券美國公債交易仍相當活躍，但低於前一日。FINRA記錄的面額交易量達$9,627億，共399,152筆，其中名目息票債交易量為$7,769億。整體面額交易量較週四下降13%，名目息票債交易量減少6.4%。三年以上至五年期債券的交易量增加5%，是所列息票債區間中唯一成長者，符合市場集中調整中期政策路徑的情況。這些數字反映的是交易周轉量，而非投資人的買賣方向。

## 長端供給與匯率政策使期限溢價居高不下

30年期公債漲幅較小，使對聯準會政策敏感的美國公債與長天期公債之間仍有明顯落差。2年期殖利率全週下跌近10個基點，30年期下跌7.2個基點，但過去一個月仍上升14.5個基點。2年與30年期利差達100.6個基點，較一個月前擴大13.6個基點。就業疲弱較容易緩解預期政策路徑，卻不足以消除長債所包含的財政、通膨及供給風險。

下一輪美國公債標售將直接檢驗這項差異。政府預定週二標售$580億3年期公債，週三標售$420億10年期公債，週四再標售$250億30年期公債。指標水準顯示，3年及10年期公債的得標殖利率可能創2025年初以來最高。30年期指標殖利率接近5.20%，高於2001年8月以來任何一次同天期標售結果；7月標售的5.058%已是2007年以來最高。

財政部在季度再融資指引中更動一個詞後，市場對未來發債期限組合的不確定性升高。官員表示正在評估附息證券標售未來可能的「變更」，取代先前所稱的未來「增加」。目前標售時程並未改變，但這項修訂促使投資人思考，財政部最終是否可能減少20年與30年期公債發行，同時增加短期及中期券種供給。

道明證券目前預期，財政部將於5月削減20年與30年期公債標售，同時擴大2年至10年期券種發行。德意志銀行策略師Steven Zeng表示，削減長債供給並非他的基本情境，因政府融資需求仍過於龐大，無法不運用整條殖利率曲線。加拿大帝國商業銀行的Michael Cloherty則認為，將供給轉向較短天期仍可能因需要更廣泛的買方群而推高相關殖利率，限制整體借貸成本的降幅。這場討論涉及未來可能採取的選項，並非已宣布的削減措施。

7月就業結果公布之際，全球投資人也正重新評估主權債券的長天期部位。威靈頓資產管理的Martin Harvey表示，他已在一檔規模$60億的全球債券基金中降低美國公債曝險，轉向包括較長天期德國公債在內的歐洲債券。威靈頓旗下全球固定收益策略也已削減主動配置的美國曝險。即使柏林準備投入€5,000億於基礎建設與國防支出，Harvey仍看好歐洲央行對通膨的因應及德國較強的財政公信力。

貝萊德的James Turner基於另一項理由，不願持有較長天期主權債券：各國地緣政治行為日益缺乏合作，期限溢價風險也更加波動。美國在7月31日干預匯市時出售歐元、買進日圓，且完成交易後才通知歐洲央行，這項揭露加深了他的疑慮。部分歐洲央行高階官員認為，在未事先協商下動用歐元，違反了西方貨幣當局既有的合作慣例。

這次干預的部分設計是避免出售美元或美國公債。日本是美國公債市場最大的外國投資人，官員一直推動使用聯準會的外國及國際貨幣當局附買回機制（FIMA），讓東京能以所持美國公債為擔保取得美元，而不必出售債券。日本財務省表示，未來干預行動可能使用該機制。高盛認為，取得FIMA機制反而展現了支撐美元儲備貨幣地位的市場深度與流動性，而非削弱其地位。

干預仍未解決匯率失衡。日圓週五早盤約報158.45兌1美元，已回吐干預後升至155.23時將近一半的漲幅。在美日進行1998年以來首次協同買進日圓之前，匯價一度接近164。市場估計日本當局首日投入約$530億，次日再投入$340億，但利差、日本債務負擔及地緣政治不確定性仍持續壓抑日圓。

干預效果消退，使官員面臨與長天期債券相似的公信力問題：市場操作可以立即改變價格，但效果能否持續，取決於背後的政策組合。隔夜指數交換顯示，日本央行9月前升息的機率約為60%。除非日本更快緊縮，或美國利率路徑轉趨溫和，干預可能仍只能帶來短暫支撐。

日本政府年金投資基金（GPIF）的表現，反映國內殖利率上升造成的資產配置壓力。截至6月的一季，GPIF獲利創紀錄的¥24.1兆，相當於$1,520億，報酬率8.2%，資產增至¥317.76兆。日本股票報酬率為14.5%，外國股票為16.9%，國內債券則虧損1.1%。儘管政府鼓勵增加國內投資，日本債券占投資組合比重仍由3月的26.91%降至25.59%。

## AI融資擴張，再融資競爭升溫

科技相關融資正成為持續性的債券供給來源，不再只是接連出現的個別超大型交易。摩根大通將2026年科技、媒體與電信業債券發行預測由$4,500億上調至$5,400億，理由是建設人工智慧基礎設施的大型企業提高支出。該行預期超大規模雲端業者將發行約$3,170億，資料中心專案融資則達$850億；若多數規劃中的交易成行，後者可能超過$1,000億。

除已完成融資的六個項目外，摩根大通另列出七個投資級資料中心融資機會，其中四個可能涉及Oracle與OpenAI。Meta預計在公布第三季業績後重返市場；Microsoft自2017年以來未曾發債，因此仍是規模最大的潛在新借款人。該行也將不含超大規模雲端業者的科技債發行預測，由$780億近乎倍增至約$1,460億。

即使新債獲得大量認購，供給也已開始影響次級市場定價。投資人於6月及7月承接約$750億的意外發行量，使部分超大規模雲端業者債券的利差擴大約15個基點。SpaceX與Amazon債券在初夏發行後表現不佳。Alphabet先前於2月發行的30年期債券，當時利差約為美國公債加83個基點，6月一度收窄至約70個基點，如今已升至100個基點以上。

Alphabet最新一筆$250億發債仍吸引約$1,150億訂單，證明高評等借款人的市場融資管道依然深厚。不過，舊債表現較弱且新債必須提供發行讓利，顯示需求對價格敏感，每筆新交易都在與流通債券競爭。Rieder認為，發行量龐大使投資級公司債缺乏吸引力；他偏好歐洲固定收益、新興市場及證券化資產，並以不犧牲流動性或信用品質為前提，尋求位於6%區間高端的殖利率。

美國科技公司增加借款之際，企業現金盈餘也在部分本地市場創造需求。SK海力士在管理AI帶動的半導體榮景所得資金時，擴大買進南韓公司債。市場人士估計，該公司今年購入10兆至40兆韓元債券，區間上端包含商業本票。

在美國存託憑證上市募得$265億挹注下，SK海力士第二季末的現金及約當現金較前季增加近62%，至88兆韓元。其投資包括評等AA以上的投資級金融及政府相關證券，期限通常不超過三年，單筆下單金額常介於1,000億至3,000億韓元。信用分析師SangIn Kim表示，這些資金流入有助避免當地信用市場出現資金緊縮。

其他市場方面，負債較重的借款人尋求降低利息支出，使公開聯貸與私人貸款之間的競爭逐漸有利於聯貸市場。摩根大通與KBRA DLD的資料顯示，原本使用私人債務的企業轉至聯貸市場再融資的頻率，約為聯貸借款人轉向私人信貸的三倍。

Catalent以$41億的美元及歐元定期貸款，取代Ares與Blue Owl提供的私人貸款，借貸成本降低約225個基點。Fidelis Partnership正規劃為約$20億的直接貸款再融資；KKR支持的Accuris預計為一筆$7億槓桿貸款定價，以償還私人貸款機構。銀行第二季完成九筆此類交易，總額$45億；同期由聯貸市場轉向直接貸款者僅三筆，總額$13億。

今年以來的累計金額則較接近。截至7月中旬，銀行主導、從私人信貸市場轉入的再融資達$92億，反方向流動約為$90億。不過，隨著企業發展公司面臨贖回及資產價值下降，銀行獲得更多競爭空間。第二季銀行持有的商業與工業貸款以年化14.2%的速度成長，一年前僅為4.4%。

並非所有借款人都能取得聯貸融資。潛在聯貸投資人要求的定價令Baker Tilly無法接受，該公司因此放棄為超過$20億私人債務再融資。這筆失敗交易限制了對整體轉向的解讀：能符合公開市場條件的借款人可取得成本較低的銀行融資；若確定性與速度比最低整體成本更重要，直接貸款仍有其價值。

QVC走出美國《破產法》第11章程序，顯示完成重整的投機級借款人仍面臨高昂債務成本。這家電視購物公司發行$12億、2032年到期且利率10%的債權人承接票據，並取得$6億資產擔保貸款額度。重整使總債務減少逾$50億，但兩位數票息顯示，一家試圖扭轉客戶流失並建立數位與社群商務業務的企業，融資成本依舊沉重。

由雪城大型購物中心Destiny USA擔保的商用不動產抵押貸款證券，壓力更為嚴重。業主Pyramid Management Group同意以每1美元面額不到20美分的價格，買回原始金額$4.3億的抵押貸款，但前提是先提供訂金並完成交易。預計損失將超過$3.5億，不過在出售完成前，最終金額仍有不確定性。

這項結構暴露了原始評等未能呈現的弱點。約$2.35億市政債券曾為購物中心提供部分融資，其受償順位高於商用不動產抵押貸款證券。然而，交易於2014年發行時，約$2.15億次順位CMBS仍獲得AAA評等，優先順位市政債務的評等反而只有單A。此後購物中心估值已下跌約四分之三；借款人於2022年未能償還抵押貸款後，進入暫緩追償安排。

市政債投資人對另一種波多黎各曝險則展現強勁需求。聖胡安發行$1.21億一般責任債券，獲逾50家機構下單，訂單總額約$22億。2051年到期的免稅債券票息為5%，發行殖利率4.9%，較基準市政債高58個基點；之後交易的平均殖利率降至4.77%。該債券由房產稅收入及部分銷售稅收入支持；2025會計年度質押的房產稅收入為$1億160萬，相較之下，有擔保債務償付額為$5,350萬。

## 主權市場獎勵財政改善、懲罰政治不確定性

南非債券市場持續反映比其非投資級評等更有利的財政路徑。南非相對無風險資產的利差收窄至約102個基點，與BBB級墨西哥相當，並低於同為BBB級的羅馬尼亞。五年期信用違約交換降至約120個基點，創15年新低；羅馬尼亞則為141個基點。

外國投資人本月淨買進236億蘭特的南非本地政府債券，使今年以來淨流入增至620億蘭特。南非財政部總司長Duncan Pieterse表示，政府仍可望在17年來首次降低債務占GDP比率，並預期該比率將於本會計年度在77.3%觸頂。

這項展望仍有爭議。IMF預測，南非債務占GDP比率明年將升至79.7%。Pieterse表示，雙方預測差距將在2月預算案公布後更加明朗，並強調政府計畫建立法定、以原則為基礎的財政規則。南非已透過發債及多邊貸款達成外幣融資目標，不打算僅因利差下降便伺機增發。

喀麥隆則傳出相反的主權信用訊號。93歲的總統Paul Biya自6月7日飛往日內瓦後一直未公開露面；該國又沒有能自動接任的副總統，繼任不確定性因而升高。喀麥隆2033年到期美元債殖利率週五升至9.53%，債券可能連續第四週下跌。

自Biya離境以來，2033年債券殖利率已上升約70個基點至約9.5%，2031年債券殖利率則上升50個基點。喀麥隆債券兩個月來下跌0.6%；同期剛果共和國債券上漲0.2%、加彭上漲1%，較廣泛的新興市場美元債指數上漲0.4%。政府表示Biya健康狀況良好並將返國，卻未提供日期。在沒有指定接班人的情況下，投資人日益反映的是權力交接所伴隨的治理風險，而非近期償債能力惡化。

墨西哥完整的7月通膨報告支持墨西哥央行將政策利率維持在6.50%的決定。整體通膨年增率由3.37%降至3.12%，符合預期；核心通膨由4.03%降至3.95%，接近3.94%的市場共識，服務類通膨則仍高達4.36%。

數據組成讓決策官員看見通膨降溫的證據，卻沒有多少理由改變審慎指引。非核心食品價格壓力消退，燃料補貼也限制了全球油價波動的影響，但服務價格已連續第56個月高於4%。墨西哥央行已將通膨回到3%目標的預估時點，由2027年第二季延後至第四季，並表示目前維持利率不變仍屬適當。

另有兩個邊境與新興市場借款人進一步說明了市場融資計畫。坦尚尼亞已全面開放非居民參與政府證券標售，並推出每日主權殖利率曲線，作為貸款與公司債定價基準。政府計畫本會計年度在國內借款3.27兆先令，相當於$12.4億；若市場條件允許，也可能發行最高$5億的歐洲債券。

巴西則要求國會授權每年在海外發行最高$350億債券，但國庫署長Daniel Leal表示，這項上限旨在保留彈性，不代表政府將立即發行如此龐大的規模。外債約占聯邦債務4%，財政部計畫逐步提高至7%。巴西今年已在全球市場發行約$100億，包括創紀錄的€50億交易，並考慮於2026年首次發行最高50億元人民幣的熊貓債。

## 能源與地緣政治阻礙通膨順利降溫

美國公債上漲之際油價反而走高，使偏弱的就業報告未能同步壓低通膨補償。WTI收於$78.18，布蘭特原油收於$83.55，兩者當日均上漲，但全週跌幅仍超過7%。這種走勢一方面反映油價自前一週極端水準明顯回落，另一方面也顯示市場仍不確定荷莫茲海峽能否以商業上可行的條件恢復通航。

伊朗國會議員討論一項提案，內容可能禁止美國與以色列船隻通行、要求敵對國家支付賠償，並收取保險及環境服務費用。伊朗也通報在海峽攻擊敵對目標，胡塞組織則宣布對葉門獲沙烏地阿拉伯支持的政府發動大規模行動。這些情況使美國總統Donald Trump所稱談判取得進展、衝突可能很快結束的說法更添變數。

週五稍晚的報導進一步指出，土耳其、沙烏地阿拉伯與巴基斯坦已在麥加簽署共同防禦協議，反映區域政府正尋求新的安全架構。阿拉伯聯合大公國的阿布達比國家石油公司表示，旗下三艘船隻本週在荷莫茲海峽遭到攻擊。胡塞組織封鎖曼德海峽航線，加上沙烏地阿拉伯西南部遇襲，形成第二條航運走廊風險，能源運輸的潛在瓶頸已不再只有荷莫茲海峽。

週末發展仍未化解問題。伊朗拒絕與美國直接談判，並重申恢復航運的條件；Trump則表示，華府可以等待經濟壓力迫使德黑蘭軟化立場。胡塞組織宣稱發動攻擊後，沙烏地阿拉伯吉贊煉油廠一度起火，火勢其後撲滅，無人受傷，一座原油儲槽受到影響。這些事件發生於美國固定收益市場完成週五收盤後，因此不是當日美國公債行情的成因，但使下一交易日仍面臨能源風險。

黃金當日上漲2.33%、全週上漲7.20%，既反映地緣政治風險未解，也受美國利率預期下降推動。美元走弱放大了漲幅，但金價在原油走強、股市創高之際同步上漲，顯示避險需求可以與廣泛的風險偏好並存。當日跨市場走勢並未形成單一的防禦性格局。

## 後續市場意義

週三公布的7月消費者物價報告，如今是檢驗就業疲弱能否延後聯準會再次升息的主要關卡。經濟學家預期，整體CPI在6月下降0.4%後將上升0.1%；核心物價預計月增0.2%、年增2.5%，後者將是2月以來最小年增幅。若結果接近預測，通膨降溫將與勞動市場轉弱形成一致訊號；若明顯高於預期，決策委員會仍須在招聘減少與通膨連續五年高於目標之間權衡。

這份數據也將檢驗週五美國公債漲勢的組成。10年期名目殖利率下降3.5個基點，但損益兩平通膨率上升0.5個基點，整體行情因此有賴實質殖利率下降4個基點。若通膨轉弱，名目殖利率的兩個組成部分都可能支持漲勢延續；若價格較強，實質殖利率的下降將面臨挑戰，也會強化部分官員的主張，即使就業處於疲弱平衡，仍有必要再次升息。

財政部總額$1,250億的再融資標售，將分別檢驗殖利率曲線三個位置的需求。週二$580億3年期公債標售，接續市場下調9月升息預期；週三$420億10年期公債標售在CPI公布後登場；週四$250億30年期公債標售，則須面對約5.2%的殖利率、持續的財政借款及公司債供給競爭。未來即使可能調整標售期限，也不會改變投資人下週必須承接的債券。

AI相關信用債仍將面臨次級市場考驗。摩根大通將科技業發債預測上調至$5,400億，加上資料中心融資可能增加，意味龐大訂單本身不足以證明供給能在毫無壓力下被市場吸收。Alphabet新債、其2月發行的30年期債券及下一筆超大規模雲端業者交易的表現，將顯示目前的發行讓利究竟能穩定流通債券，還是只能用更高成本完成每筆新發行。

私人信貸轉向聯貸市場的趨勢，也即將接受實際交易檢驗。Accuris預計下週為$7億再融資交易定價，Fidelis則正尋求以新融資取代約$20億直接貸款。如果兩筆交易能以具競爭力的條件完成，將支持銀行因企業重視降低借貸成本而重新取得市占的看法；若再出現Baker Tilly式的撤案，便顯示公開市場的成本節省仍取決於槓桿程度、交易條款及投資人承受意願。

澳洲央行將於週二議息，經濟學家與交易員預期現金利率連續第二次會議維持在4.35%。市場焦點是，在今年累計升息75個基點後，更新後的預測及總裁Michele Bullock記者會是否仍保留緊縮傾向。貨幣市場反映年底前再升息25個基點的機率約為50%至60%，分析師則對通膨放緩及房市轉弱能否讓利率維持不變看法不一。

荷莫茲海峽仍是通膨前景變化最快的威脅。真正重要的進展並非再次聲稱談判有所推進，而是達成具體安排，明訂哪些船隻可以通行、須支付哪些費用或賠償、保險公司是否認為航線安全，以及荷莫茲海峽與紅海的攻擊是否停止。週末伊朗拒絕與美國直接談判，加上胡塞組織宣稱攻擊吉贊煉油廠，使亞洲交易開始時這些條件仍未獲滿足。

日本匯率政策也對全球長天期債券形成相關考驗。日圓已回吐干預後近一半漲幅，使160兌1美元附近成為市場焦點，也提高再次干預的可能性。後續任何行動都將取決於日本央行是否釋出更強烈的政策訊號，以及日本會使用聯準會FIMA機制、還是出售美國公債。干預仍可迅速改變即期匯率，但效果能否持續，仍取決於美日利差及整體政策組合的公信力。

overall_summary.headline: 就業減少使聯準會升息討論延後，美國公債上漲、殖利率曲線轉陡
overall_summary.session_narrative:
美國7月非農就業未如預期增加約8萬人，反而減少2.3萬人，5月與6月數據又合計下修10.3萬人，帶動美國公債上漲。2年期殖利率下降5.3個基點至4.196%，10年期下降3.5個基點至4.646%，30年期下跌2.5個基點至5.202%。短端跌幅較大，使2年與10年期利差擴至45個基點，2年與30年期利差擴至100.6個基點；9月升息機率則由近60%降至約40%。

這份報告削弱了立即緊縮的理由，卻未解決通膨問題。勞動參與率下降，協助失業率降至4.1%；薪資成長放緩，多個產業也減少職位，但投資人仍完全反映年底前升息一次。10年期實質殖利率下降4個基點，損益兩平通膨率反而上升0.5個基點，顯示美國公債行情來自成長與政策利率預期下調，而非通膨壓力緩解。

股市升至歷史新高，信用債基金上漲，美元走弱，反映市場主要將招聘降溫視為聯準會可以等待的理由，而非經濟急遽萎縮的證據。油價上漲，加上美國公債與公司債供給壓力持續，使長天期債券仍要求較高補償，30年期殖利率因而維持在5.2%以上。

## Opening Fixed-Income Thesis

Treasuries rallied on Aug. 7 after the US unexpectedly lost jobs in July and large downward revisions showed that the preceding months had been weaker than first reported. The surprise removed some urgency from the Federal Reserve’s tightening debate without eliminating it: the 2-year yield fell 5.3 basis points to 4.196%, the 5-year declined 4.4 basis points to 4.353%, the 10-year dropped 3.5 basis points to 4.646% and the 30-year eased 2.5 basis points to 5.202%.

The stronger front-end response steepened the curve. The 2s10s spread widened 1.8 basis points to 45 basis points, while 2s30s increased 2.8 basis points to 100.6 basis points. Investors reduced the probability of a September rate increase to roughly 40% from almost 60% before the employment report, but still fully priced a move by year-end. The distinction reflected a labor release that weakened the case for immediate tightening while leaving inflation, fiscal supply and the credibility of the Fed’s response concentrated farther out the curve.

Nonfarm payrolls fell 23,000 against expectations for an increase of about 80,000, and May and June were revised down by a combined 103,000. The unemployment rate nevertheless declined to 4.1% because labor-force participation fell, while wage growth slowed. Job losses in government, leisure and hospitality and retail trade added breadth to the negative headline. Richmond Fed President Tom Barkin described the labor market as being in a “weak balance” and said he was not seeing wage inflation, but retained the possibility that rates would have to rise if price pressure accelerated.

The composition of the Treasury move reinforced that conditional interpretation. The 10-year real yield fell 4 basis points to 2.392%, accounting for more than the decline in the nominal yield, while the 10-year breakeven rose 0.5 basis point to 2.254%. The market therefore marked down the real-rate path associated with growth and monetary restraint but did not receive comparable inflation relief. WTI rose 1.15% to $78.18 and Brent gained 1.29% to $83.55 as negotiations over the Strait of Hormuz remained unresolved, even though both contracts finished more than 7% lower over the week.

Risk assets treated weaker hiring chiefly as permission for the Fed to wait, rather than evidence that the economy was entering an abrupt contraction. The S&P 500 rose 0.62% to a record and completed a 3.58% weekly advance. The Nasdaq 100 gained 1.19%, and the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index climbed 2.56%. The dollar index fell 0.37%, while gold futures rose 2.33% to $4,340.70. Treasury yields declined alongside stronger equities and firmer oil, making the policy repricing—not a generalized retreat from risk—the defining feature of the close.

The rally did not repair the longer-term duration problem. The 30-year yield remained above 5.2% and had risen 14.5 basis points over one month, compared with an increase of only 0.9 basis point at 2 years. Debate over future Treasury auction sizes, heavy technology issuance and the uncertain inflation consequences of the Iran conflict continued to demand compensation at the long end. Payrolls changed the near-term Fed calculation; they did not settle the price of long-dated capital.

## Payroll Losses Reopen the Labor Side of the Fed Debate

The July employment report materially changed the measured state of the labor market. A decline of 23,000 payrolls was not merely a miss against the expected increase of about 80,000. The combined 103,000 reduction to May and June showed that the earlier trajectory had also been overstated, bringing average job growth over the latest three months to roughly 20,000. That sequence made the report harder to dismiss as an isolated monthly fluctuation.

The sector detail pointed to more than one source of weakness. Government employment declined, while leisure and hospitality and retail trade also cut jobs. Those losses mattered because they extended beyond a single industry exposed to a temporary disruption. At the same time, the fall in unemployment to 4.1% prevented the release from becoming an unambiguous recession signal. Participation continued to slide, reducing the number of people counted in the labor force and helping explain why the jobless rate improved even as payrolls contracted.

Slower wage growth reinforced the case that labor demand was no longer adding the same inflation pressure. Barkin said the result was consistent with the low-hire environment that has prevailed for about a year and a half: the market was neither loose nor tight, but in a weak balance. He said he was not seeing wage inflation and did not believe employment conditions were currently contributing to price pressure.

Barkin, who votes on policy next year, did not convert that assessment into an unconditional case against higher rates. A week earlier, he had described the question of whether borrowing costs were high enough to restrain inflation as a close call. On Friday, he said officials might still need to tighten if inflationary headwinds intensified. His position therefore separated two questions that the market had recently treated together: a weak hiring environment reduces the risk of labor-driven inflation, but it does not ensure that energy, trade costs or other prices will return to target.

The reaction in short rates captured that distinction. Two-year yields fell as much as 9 basis points after the data before ending 5.3 basis points lower. Traders cut the probability of a September increase to around 40%, compared with close to 60% before the report. Hedges against higher short-term rates were unwound in options tied to the Secured Overnight Financing Rate, although investors continued to price one increase by year-end and retained protection against another move in 2027.

The persistence of a year-end increase reflects both uncertainty in monthly employment data and the unresolved inflation problem. Three officials dissented from the Fed’s July decision to keep its target range at 3.5% to 3.75%, preferring a quarter-point increase. Inflation remains above the 2% objective, and Chair Kevin Warsh has offered little guidance about the conditions that would turn a hold into a hike. Payrolls made a September move harder to justify, but did not establish how much inflation improvement the committee will require before abandoning tightening altogether.

The New York Fed’s July consumer survey added a more complicated household view. Workers’ perceived probability of finding a new job if unemployed rose to 46.2%, the highest this year, with particularly large increases among respondents with a high-school education or less and households earning below $50,000. Yet respondents also assigned a greater probability to unemployment being higher one year ahead, and their perceived chance of losing a job edged up.

Household inflation expectations improved modestly at the shortest horizon. The expected one-year inflation rate fell to 3.6% from 3.7%, while the three-year and five-year measures remained at 3.3% and 3%. More households said their current finances were better than a year earlier, but the perceived probability of missing a minimum debt payment over the coming three months rose, especially for lower-income households. The survey preceded the payroll release and did not erase its signal; it showed that consumers were still experiencing a labor market with available opportunities alongside greater concern about the broader outlook.

BlackRock’s Rick Rieder supplied a material counterinterpretation of the payroll decline. He argued that weak hiring reflected a productivity transformation rather than an economy losing momentum, citing artificial-intelligence adoption, corporate efficiency and lower immigration as reasons firms could expand without adding workers. Rieder continued to expect about 6% nominal GDP growth and described the economy as broadly unimpressive rather than weak.

That distinction matters for policy because slower headcount growth need not imply a proportional loss of output or demand. If productivity is allowing companies to produce more with fewer employees, payroll weakness may overstate the deterioration in activity. Rieder also argued that higher overnight rates were poorly suited to restraining sticky prices in health care, insurance and education, favoring fiscal and regulatory measures instead. His assessment challenges both sides of the conventional reaction function: the jobs report may not signal severe growth weakness, and another rate increase may not directly address the sources of persistent inflation.

The cross-market response leaned toward the benign interpretation. Stocks rose rather than falling on concern about lost income, with technology and semiconductor shares leading. The dollar declined against all its major peers as near-term Fed expectations softened. Credit funds also advanced modestly: LQD gained 0.18%, HYG rose 0.19%, JNK added 0.21% and EMB increased 0.31%. Those price moves showed that investors regarded policy patience as more important for the session than the possibility that employment weakness would impair corporate cash flow.

Cash Treasury activity was substantial but lower than the previous session. FINRA recorded $962.7 billion of par trading across 399,152 transactions, with nominal-coupon activity at $776.9 billion. Overall par volume fell 13% from Thursday, and nominal-coupon activity declined 6.4%. Trading in maturities longer than 3 years through 5 years increased 5%, the only listed coupon sector to record higher activity, consistent with concentrated adjustment around the intermediate policy path. The figures describe turnover rather than investor direction.

## Long-End Supply and Currency Policy Keep Duration Premiums Elevated

The smaller rally at 30 years preserved a steep divide between Fed-sensitive and long-duration Treasuries. The 2-year yield was almost 10 basis points lower over the week, while the 30-year fell 7.2 basis points and remained 14.5 basis points higher over one month. The 2s30s curve reached 100.6 basis points, 13.6 basis points wider than a month earlier. Payroll weakness relieved the expected policy path more readily than the fiscal, inflation and supply risks embedded in long bonds.

The next Treasury auctions will test that separation directly. The government is scheduled to sell $58 billion of 3-year notes on Tuesday, $42 billion of 10-year notes on Wednesday and $25 billion of 30-year bonds on Thursday. Indicated levels suggested the 3- and 10-year securities could draw their highest auction yields since early 2025. The 30-year was indicated near 5.20%, above the result of any auction for that maturity since August 2001; July’s 5.058% result was already the highest since 2007.

Uncertainty about the future maturity mix has grown since Treasury changed one word in its quarterly refunding guidance. Officials said they were evaluating possible future “changes” to auctions of interest-bearing securities, replacing the previous reference to future “increases.” The current auction schedule did not change, but the revision prompted investors to consider whether Treasury might eventually reduce 20- and 30-year sales while increasing shorter and intermediate maturities.

TD Securities now expects cuts to 20- and 30-year auctions in May, alongside larger sales of 2- to 10-year notes. Deutsche Bank strategist Steven Zeng said reductions were not his base case because the government’s financing needs remained too large to avoid using the full curve. CIBC’s Michael Cloherty argued that shifting supply toward shorter maturities could still raise their yields by requiring a wider buyer base, limiting any reduction in overall borrowing costs. The debate concerns a possible future choice, not an announced cut.

The July payroll result also arrived against a more global reconsideration of sovereign duration. Wellington Asset Management’s Martin Harvey said he had reduced Treasury exposure in a $6 billion global bond fund and shifted toward European debt, including longer-dated German bonds. Across Wellington’s global fixed-income strategies, active US exposure had also been cut. Harvey cited the European Central Bank’s inflation response and Germany’s stronger fiscal credibility, even as Berlin prepares €500 billion of infrastructure and defense spending.

BlackRock’s James Turner was reluctant to hold longer sovereign duration for a different reason: geopolitical behavior was becoming less cooperative and term-premium risk more volatile. His concern followed the disclosure that the US sold euros to buy yen during the July 31 intervention and notified the European Central Bank only after the transaction. Some senior ECB officials regarded the use of euros without prior consultation as a breach of established cooperation among Western monetary authorities.

The intervention was structured partly to avoid selling dollars or Treasuries. Japan is the largest foreign investor in the Treasury market, and officials have promoted the Fed’s Foreign and International Monetary Authorities Repo Facility as a way for Tokyo to obtain dollars against its Treasury holdings rather than liquidate them. Japan’s Finance Ministry has indicated that the facility could be used in future operations. Goldman Sachs argued that access to FIMA demonstrates the depth and liquidity supporting the dollar’s reserve role rather than weakening it.

The operation has not resolved the currency imbalance. The yen traded around 158.45 per dollar on Friday morning, having surrendered almost half its gain from a strong point of 155.23 after the intervention. It had been near 164 before the first coordinated yen purchase by the US and Japan since 1998. Japanese authorities were estimated to have spent about $53 billion on the first day and $34 billion on the second, yet the interest-rate differential, Japan’s debt load and geopolitical uncertainty continued to weigh on the currency.

The fading effect leaves officials with a credibility problem similar to the one facing long-duration bonds: a market operation can alter the immediate price, but its persistence depends on the underlying policy mix. Overnight-index swaps assigned about a 60% probability to a Bank of Japan increase by September. Without faster Japanese tightening or a softer US rate path, intervention may continue to provide only temporary relief.

Japan’s Government Pension Investment Fund illustrated the allocation pressure created by higher domestic yields. GPIF earned a record ¥24.1 trillion, or $152 billion, in the quarter through June, an 8.2% return that lifted assets to ¥317.76 trillion. Japanese equities returned 14.5% and foreign shares 16.9%, while domestic bonds lost 1.1%. The share of Japanese bonds in the portfolio fell to 25.59% from 26.91% in March, despite government efforts to encourage more domestic investment.

## AI Borrowing Expands as Refinancing Competition Intensifies

Technology-related borrowing is becoming a persistent source of supply rather than a sequence of isolated jumbo transactions. JPMorgan raised its forecast for 2026 technology, media and telecommunications debt issuance to $540 billion from $450 billion, citing higher spending by the largest companies building artificial-intelligence infrastructure. The bank expects hyperscalers to account for about $317 billion and data-center project finance for $85 billion, with the latter potentially exceeding $100 billion if most planned transactions proceed.

JPMorgan identified seven investment-grade data-center opportunities beyond the six already funded. Four could involve Oracle and OpenAI, Meta is expected to return after reporting Q3 results, and Microsoft remains the largest potential new borrower because it has not tapped the bond market since 2017. The bank also nearly doubled its forecast for technology issuance excluding hyperscalers to about $146 billion from $78 billion.

The supply has begun to affect secondary pricing even when new deals attract large orderbooks. Investors absorbed about $75 billion of unexpected issuance in June and July, widening spreads on some hyperscaler debt by roughly 15 basis points. SpaceX and Amazon bonds traded poorly after issuance earlier in the summer. Alphabet’s previously issued 30-year bond, sold in February at a spread of about 83 basis points over Treasuries, was trading above 100 basis points after reaching about 70 in June.

Alphabet’s latest $25 billion sale still drew about $115 billion of orders, proving that market access remains deep for highly rated borrowers. The weaker performance of older bonds and the need for new-issue concessions showed that demand is price-sensitive and that each transaction competes with outstanding paper. Rieder described investment-grade corporate credit as uninteresting because of the volume arriving, preferring European fixed income, emerging markets and securitized assets while targeting yields in the high 6% range without sacrificing liquidity or credit quality.

Corporate cash surpluses are creating demand in some local markets even as US technology companies become heavier borrowers. SK Hynix has expanded purchases of South Korean corporate bonds while managing the proceeds from the AI-driven semiconductor boom. Market participants estimated that the company bought between 10 trillion won and 40 trillion won of bonds this year, with the upper figure including commercial paper.

Its cash and equivalents increased almost 62% from the previous quarter to 88 trillion won at the end of Q2, aided by $26.5 billion from a US depositary-receipt listing. Purchases have included investment-grade financial and government-related securities rated above AA, generally with maturities of no more than three years. Individual orders were often between 100 billion won and 300 billion won. Credit analyst SangIn Kim said the inflow had helped prevent a squeeze in the local credit market.

Elsewhere, the competition between public and private lending is moving in favor of syndicated loans as indebted borrowers seek to reduce interest expense. Companies with private debt are refinancing in the syndicated market about three times as often as syndicated borrowers are moving into private credit, according to JPMorgan and KBRA DLD data.

Catalent replaced private loans from Ares and Blue Owl with $4.1 billion of dollar and euro term loans, cutting borrowing costs by about 225 basis points. Fidelis Partnership is working on refinancing roughly $2 billion of direct loans, and KKR-backed Accuris is scheduled to price a $700 million leveraged loan that would repay private lenders. Banks completed nine such transactions totaling $4.5 billion in Q2, compared with three deals worth $1.3 billion moving from syndicated markets to direct lenders.

The year-to-date totals were closer: bank-led refinancings taken from private credit reached $9.2 billion through mid-July, while about $9 billion moved in the opposite direction. Banks nevertheless gained room to compete as business-development companies experienced withdrawals and lower asset values. Commercial and industrial loans held by banks grew at a 14.2% annualized rate in Q2, compared with 4.4% one year earlier.

Access is not universal. Baker Tilly abandoned an attempt to refinance more than $2 billion of private debt after prospective syndicated-loan investors demanded pricing the company considered unacceptable. The failed transaction qualified the broader shift: cheaper bank financing is available to borrowers that can meet public-market terms, while direct loans retain their value when certainty and speed matter more than the lowest all-in cost.

QVC’s emergence from Chapter 11 showed how expensive debt remains for a reorganized speculative borrower. The shopping network issued $1.2 billion of take-back notes due in 2032 with a 10% interest rate and obtained a $600 million asset-based lending facility. The restructuring reduced total debt by more than $5 billion, but the double-digit coupon indicates the continuing cost of funding a business trying to reverse customer losses and build a digital and social-commerce presence.

Stress was more severe in commercial mortgage bonds backed by Destiny USA, the Syracuse megamall. Owner Pyramid Management Group agreed to buy back the original $430 million mortgage for less than 20 cents on the dollar, subject to providing a deposit and completing the transaction. Losses are expected to exceed $350 million, although the final amount remains uncertain until the sale closes.

The structure exposed a weakness that original ratings had obscured. About $235 million of municipal bonds financed part of the mall and rank ahead of the commercial mortgage securities. Some $215 million of subordinated CMBS had nevertheless received AAA ratings when the deal was issued in 2014, while the senior municipal debt was rated single-A. The mall’s appraised value has since fallen by about three-quarters, and the borrower entered forbearance after failing to repay the mortgage in 2022.

Municipal investors showed strong demand for a different kind of Puerto Rico exposure. San Juan received about $2.2 billion of orders from more than 50 firms for a $121 million general-obligation sale. Tax-exempt bonds due in 2051 were issued with a 5% coupon at a 4.9% yield, 58 basis points above benchmark municipal debt, and subsequently traded at an average yield of 4.77%. The debt is supported by property-tax collections and part of sales-tax revenue; pledged property-tax collections totaled $101.6 million in fiscal 2025 against $53.5 million of secured debt service.

## Sovereign Markets Reward Fiscal Progress and Penalize Political Uncertainty

South Africa’s bond market continued to price a more favorable fiscal trajectory than its sub-investment-grade ratings imply. The country’s spread over risk-free assets narrowed to about 102 basis points, comparable with BBB-rated Mexico and below BBB- rated Romania. Five-year credit-default swaps fell to a 15-year low near 120 basis points, versus 141 for Romania.

Foreign investors bought a net 23.6 billion rand of local government bonds during the month, lifting year-to-date inflows to 62 billion rand. Treasury Director-General Duncan Pieterse said the government remained on course to reduce debt relative to GDP for the first time in 17 years and expected the ratio to peak at 77.3% in the current fiscal year.

That outlook remains disputed. The IMF projected debt would rise to 79.7% of GDP next year. Pieterse said the difference would become clearer with February’s budget and emphasized plans for a statutory, principles-based fiscal rule. South Africa has already met its foreign-currency borrowing target through bonds and multilateral loans and does not intend to issue opportunistically merely because spreads have declined.

Cameroon supplied the opposite sovereign-credit signal. President Paul Biya, 93, had not appeared publicly since flying to Geneva on June 7, intensifying uncertainty about succession in a country without a vice president to assume power automatically. The yield on Cameroon’s 2033 dollar bonds rose to 9.53% on Friday, leaving the securities on course for a fourth consecutive weekly loss.

Since Biya left the country, the 2033 yield has climbed about 70 basis points to roughly 9.5%, while 2031 yields increased 50 basis points. Cameroon’s debt lost 0.6% over two months, compared with gains of 0.2% for the Republic of Congo, 1% for Gabon and 0.4% for a broader emerging-market dollar-bond index. The government said Biya was in good health and would return, but gave no date. With no named successor, investors were increasingly pricing the governance risk surrounding a transition rather than a deterioration in near-term debt service.

Mexico’s completed July inflation report reinforced Banxico’s decision to hold its policy rate at 6.50%. Annual headline inflation slowed to 3.12% from 3.37%, matching expectations. Core inflation eased to 3.95% from 4.03%, close to the 3.94% consensus, while services inflation remained elevated at 4.36%.

The composition left policymakers with evidence of disinflation but little reason to reverse their cautious guidance. Non-core food pressure faded and fuel subsidies limited the impact of global oil swings, while services prices remained above 4% for a 56th consecutive month. Banxico has pushed its expected return to the 3% target to Q4 2027 from Q2 2027 and indicated that keeping rates at the current level remains appropriate.

Two frontier and emerging borrowers also clarified their market-access plans. Tanzania opened government-security auctions fully to non-residents and introduced a daily sovereign yield curve intended to provide a pricing benchmark for loans and corporate bonds. The government plans to borrow 3.27 trillion shillings, or $1.24 billion, domestically this fiscal year and may sell a Eurobond of as much as $500 million if conditions permit.

Brazil, meanwhile, asked Congress for authorization to issue as much as $35 billion a year abroad, but Treasury Secretary Daniel Leal said the ceiling was designed to create flexibility rather than signal immediate sales of that size. Foreign bonds account for about 4% of federal debt, and the Treasury aims to raise that share gradually toward 7%. Brazil has issued about $10 billion globally this year, including a record €5 billion transaction, and is considering an inaugural Panda bond of as much as 5 billion yuan in 2026.

## Energy and Geopolitics Resist a Clean Disinflation Story

The Treasury rally occurred while oil rose, preventing the jobs report from delivering a parallel decline in inflation compensation. WTI finished at $78.18 and Brent at $83.55, both higher on the day but more than 7% lower over the week. The pattern reflected substantial relief from the previous week’s extremes alongside persistent uncertainty about whether the Strait of Hormuz would reopen on commercially usable terms.

Iranian lawmakers debated a proposal that could bar US and Israeli vessels, demand compensation from hostile countries and impose fees for insurance and environmental services. Iran also reported attacks on hostile targets in the strait, while the Houthis announced a large-scale operation against Yemen’s Saudi-backed government. Those conditions complicated President Donald Trump’s statement that negotiations were progressing and that the conflict could end soon.

The later Friday account added that Turkey, Saudi Arabia and Pakistan had signed a mutual-defense agreement in Mecca as regional governments sought a new security framework. The United Arab Emirates’ Adnoc said three of its vessels had been attacked in Hormuz during the week. The Houthi closure of the Bab el-Mandeb route and strikes in southwestern Saudi Arabia created a second corridor risk rather than leaving Hormuz as the only potential constraint on energy traffic.

Events over the weekend did not resolve the issue. Iran rejected direct talks with the US and reiterated conditions for restoring shipping, while Trump said Washington could wait for economic pressure to soften Tehran’s position. A fire at Saudi Arabia’s Jazan refinery was extinguished after the Houthis claimed an attack; no injuries were reported, and one crude-storage tank was affected. These developments occurred after the completed US fixed-income close and therefore did not cause Friday’s Treasury move, but they preserve energy risk for the next session.

Gold’s 2.33% daily rise and 7.20% weekly gain reflected that unresolved geopolitical backdrop as well as the decline in US rate expectations. The dollar’s fall amplified the move, but gold’s strength alongside firmer crude and record equities showed that demand for protection remained compatible with broad risk-taking. The session did not produce a single defensive cross-market pattern.

## Forward Market Significance

The July consumer-price report on Wednesday is now the principal test of whether payroll weakness can delay the next Fed increase. Economists expect headline CPI to rise 0.1% after a 0.4% decline in June, while core prices are projected to increase 0.2% on the month and 2.5% from a year earlier, the smallest annual core gain since February. A result near those forecasts would add inflation moderation to the weaker labor picture. A material upside surprise would leave the committee weighing reduced hiring against price pressure that has persisted despite five years above target.

The data will also test the composition of Friday’s Treasury rally. The 10-year nominal yield fell 3.5 basis points even though breakeven inflation rose 0.5 basis point, leaving the move dependent on a 4-basis-point decline in the real yield. Softer inflation could extend the rally through both components. Firmer prices would challenge the real-rate decline and strengthen the argument of officials who regard another increase as necessary even with employment in weak balance.

Treasury’s $125 billion refunding sequence will examine demand at three distinct points on the curve. Tuesday’s $58 billion 3-year sale follows the reduction in September hike expectations. Wednesday’s $42 billion 10-year auction comes after CPI. Thursday’s $25 billion 30-year sale confronts a yield around 5.2%, persistent fiscal borrowing and competition from corporate supply. The possible future alteration of auction maturities does not change the securities investors must absorb next week.

AI-related credit faces a continuing secondary-market test. JPMorgan’s revised $540 billion technology issuance forecast and the prospect of more data-center finance mean that a large orderbook alone will not establish that supply is being absorbed without strain. The behavior of Alphabet’s new bonds, its February 30-year issue and the next hyperscaler transaction will show whether current concessions stabilize outstanding debt or merely clear each new offering at a higher cost.

The shift from private credit to syndicated loans also has an immediate transaction test. Accuris is expected to price a $700 million refinancing next week, while Fidelis is pursuing a roughly $2 billion replacement of direct loans. Competitive execution would support the view that banks are regaining share as companies prioritize lower borrowing costs. Another withdrawal like Baker Tilly’s would show that public-market savings remain conditional on leverage, terms and investor tolerance.

The Reserve Bank of Australia decides on Tuesday, with economists and traders expecting the cash rate to remain at 4.35% for a second meeting. The focus is whether updated forecasts and Governor Michele Bullock’s press conference retain a tightening bias after 75 basis points of increases this year. Money markets assign roughly a 50%-to-60% probability to another quarter-point move by year-end, while analysts disagree on whether slower inflation and a weakening housing market will allow rates to remain unchanged.

Hormuz remains the fastest-moving threat to the inflation outlook. The relevant development is not another statement that talks are progressing, but an arrangement that establishes which ships may pass, what fees or compensation apply, whether insurers regard the route as safe and whether attacks cease in Hormuz and the Red Sea. The weekend rejection of direct US talks and the claimed strike on the Jazan refinery leave those conditions unmet as Asian trading begins.

Japan’s currency policy presents a related test for global duration. The yen’s loss of almost half its intervention gain leaves the 160-per-dollar area in focus and raises the possibility of renewed action. Any further operation will be judged by whether it is accompanied by a stronger Bank of Japan policy signal and whether Japan uses the Fed’s FIMA facility rather than selling Treasuries. Intervention can again alter the spot rate quickly; durability still depends on the US-Japan rate differential and the credibility of the broader policy mix.

section_summaries.market_read: Payroll weakness changed near-term policy pricing more than the inflation and supply risks embedded in long yields.
section_summaries.summary: Weak payrolls and substantial downward revisions produced a front-end-led Treasury rally and steeper curves by reducing the urgency of a September Fed increase. The move reflected lower real-rate expectations rather than inflation relief, while firm oil, fiscal supply and heavy corporate issuance preserved pressure on long-duration bonds.

section_summaries.market_read: Stocks, credit and the dollar showed that policy patience outweighed concern that weaker hiring signaled an abrupt contraction.
section_summaries.section_title: Payroll Losses Reopen the Labor Side of the Fed Debate
section_summaries.summary: July payrolls fell 23,000, prior months were revised down by 103,000 and three-month average job growth slowed to roughly 20,000. Falling participation helped unemployment decline to 4.1%, while slower wages and broad sector losses reduced labor-driven inflation concerns. Barkin still left room to tighten if other price pressures intensified, and Rieder argued that productivity gains may allow output to grow despite weak hiring.

section_summaries.market_read: Near-term policy relief did not remove the compensation demanded for fiscal borrowing, geopolitical risk and long-end supply.
section_summaries.section_title: Long-End Supply and Currency Policy Keep Duration Premiums Elevated
section_summaries.summary: The smaller 30-year rally preserved a steep divide between Fed-sensitive and long-duration Treasuries ahead of $125 billion of 3-, 10- and 30-year auctions. Possible future changes to Treasury’s maturity mix remain under debate rather than announced. Reduced Treasury exposure among global managers and the yen’s fading intervention gain also underscored concern about fiscal credibility, term premiums and the durability of policy operations.

section_summaries.market_read: Each large technology deal competes with outstanding bonds, while bank refinancing remains available only at acceptable public-market terms.
section_summaries.section_title: AI Borrowing Expands as Refinancing Competition Intensifies
section_summaries.summary: JPMorgan raised its 2026 technology debt-issuance forecast to $540 billion as hyperscaler and data-center spending expands. Large orderbooks still coexist with wider secondary spreads and new-issue concessions, showing that demand is price-sensitive. Syndicated loans are also reclaiming some refinancings from private credit, although Baker Tilly’s abandoned deal showed that savings depend on leverage, terms and investor tolerance.

section_summaries.market_read: Sovereign pricing distinguished improving fiscal credibility from governance uncertainty even where near-term debt service had not changed.
section_summaries.section_title: Sovereign Markets Reward Fiscal Progress and Penalize Political Uncertainty
section_summaries.summary: South African bonds benefited from foreign inflows and expectations that debt will peak, though the IMF projects a less favorable path. Cameroon’s dollar bonds weakened as President Paul Biya’s absence intensified succession uncertainty. Mexico’s inflation slowdown supported Banxico’s hold at 6.50%, while persistent services inflation reinforced its cautious guidance.

section_summaries.market_read: Firmer crude helped prevent the payroll-led Treasury rally from producing comparable relief in inflation compensation.
section_summaries.section_title: Energy and Geopolitics Resist a Clean Disinflation Story
section_summaries.summary: Oil rose despite finishing more than 7% lower for the week as negotiations failed to establish commercially reliable passage through the Strait of Hormuz. Proposed restrictions, attacks and a second corridor risk around Bab el-Mandeb preserved uncertainty over energy traffic. Gold also advanced as weaker US rate expectations and geopolitical protection demand coexisted with record equities.

July CPI will test whether weaker labor data can delay another Fed increase and whether Friday’s real-yield-led rally can broaden. The $125 billion Treasury refunding will test demand across the curve, while Hormuz access remains the fastest-moving inflation risk. Technology issuance, syndicated refinancings, the RBA decision and the durability of yen intervention provide additional tests of credit and global policy transmission.

overall_summary.headline: Treasuries rally and curves steepen as payroll losses delay the Fed debate
overall_summary.session_narrative:
Treasuries rallied after payrolls fell 23,000 in July instead of rising by about 80,000, while May and June were revised down by a combined 103,000. The 2-year yield declined 5.3 basis points to 4.196%, the 10-year fell 3.5 basis points to 4.646% and the 30-year eased 2.5 basis points to 5.202%. The larger front-end move widened 2s10s to 45 basis points and 2s30s to 100.6 basis points as the probability of a September rate increase dropped to roughly 40% from almost 60%.

The report weakened the case for immediate tightening without resolving inflation. Falling participation helped unemployment decline to 4.1%, wage growth slowed and several sectors lost jobs, but investors still fully priced an increase by year-end. The 10-year real yield fell 4 basis points while the breakeven rose 0.5 basis point, showing that lower growth and policy-rate expectations, rather than inflation relief, drove the Treasury move.

Equities rose to records, credit funds advanced and the dollar weakened, indicating that markets treated softer hiring chiefly as permission for the Fed to wait rather than as evidence of abrupt contraction. Firmer oil and persistent Treasury and corporate supply kept long-duration compensation elevated, leaving the 30-year yield above 5.2%.
overall_summary.summary: An unexpected 23,000 decline in July payrolls and large downward revisions reduced the urgency of another Fed increase, pulling short yields lower while inflation, energy and supply risks limited the long-end rally.
